learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra.
Ability to abstract: ability to create and use models that reflect real situations.
Use the basic properties of real and complex numbers and perform fundamental operations with them.
Use the basic elements of Linear Algebra: systems of linear equations, vector spaces and linear applications and use matrices to simplify their study.
Identify metric properties in vector spaces, through the scalar product, norm, or distance.
Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors and diagonalize endomorphisms and matrices.
Solve geometric problems in the plane and space.
Identify the basic elements of differential equations and systems of differential equations and use algebraic tools to solve elementary cases.

syllabus_topics: Resolución de sistemas a través del Método de Gauss.
Combinaciones lineales e independencia lineal. Bases y dimensión. Coordenadas.
Núcleo e imagen de una aplicación. Clasificación.
Diagonalización de endomorfismos y matrices y aplicaciones.
Diagnalización de endomorfismos en bases ortonormales.
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.15 NL + max(0.15 NA + 0.7 NC, 0.85 NC), where NL is the laboratory practices grade, NA is the classroom practices grade, and NC = (P1 + P2)/2 is the average grade of the partial exams. To pass, NF must be >= 5, NL >= 3, and NC >= 3; otherwise, the final grade will be min(NF, 4.5). For classroom practices, attendance to at least 80% of programmed sessions is required. In extraordinary calls, students can improve NC and/or NL through written exams or laboratory practice tests, retaining the other grade if only one part is repeated.
